scale_derivation.factor_name: kitchen source px (10-kitchen.webp 1712x1232) -> furniture px at the Royal/in-game scale (hex 791, 1 px = 0.1730239 world)
how: The original kitchen is a perspective photo, not an in-hex picture. The pipeline composed it onto the SAME locked template as the Royal and nursery rooms (kitchen-clean-in-game-hex-meta.json: src_verts TL(520,615) TR(1300,598) R(1575,840) BR(1420,1215) BL(400,1215) L(95,905) -> dst_floor, hex width 790.97).

SIFT (20000 features, ratio 0.75, RANSAC affine) between 10-kitchen.webp and kitchen-clean-in-game-hex-no-outline.jpg on objects that were composed unscaled (scenery kept in the clean in-hex picture): utensil_rack: sx 0.5120 sy 0.7873 (131 inliers); grapes_back: sx 0.5071 sy 0.7762 (95 inliers); back_left_shelf: sx 0.4989 sy 0.7719 (79 inliers); lantern_back_left: sx 0.4963 sy 0.7706 (16 inliers); lantern_back_right: sx 0.5152 sy 0.7861 (19 inliers). Median horizontal scale 0.5071 -> used as the uniform factor.
Cross-check on the floor: compose floor homography x-scale at the furniture feet = 0.512 (stove), 0.539 (table), 0.561 (sink), 0.537 (straw), 0.518 (jar).

Cross-check with the recorded scale pass: kitchen scale-v1/v1b used 0.16 x source px for an Albert ~45 px tall (NOTE-scale-v1b scale_note). Re-targeting that to Albert 130 px gives 0.16 x 130/45 = 0.462, within 9% of 0.5071.
Uniform (aspect-preserving) scale: the compose stretches wall objects vertically (sy ~0.78 vs sx ~0.51); I did not stretch, so heights follow the width scale.
scale_derivation.not_used: scale-v1/v1b sprites (0.16) - shrunk for the old ~45 px ant
